summary: Understand the real problem: listen to customers, explore their frustrations and establish what needs to change.
Uncover hidden opportunities: connect conversations across teams to find challenges the business has not yet recognised.
Turn discovery into sales: build a clear case for action and shape opportunities into valuable customer engagements.
Make AI practical: prioritise use cases and roadmaps around business value, workflows and the data foundations they need.
Connect customers and strategy: bring frontline insight into demonstrations, propositions and go-to-market decisions.
detail: My recent pre-sales experience starts with the customer’s situation: what is difficult, where time is lost, what frustrates people and what happens if nothing changes. I explore the implications and the need before considering whether AI has a useful role. That gives the conversation a clear business purpose and helps establish trust with the people who live with the problem.

The opportunity often becomes clearer as different teams share their perspective. At Keltbray, conversations with the finance team identified five challenges, including issues their data team had not been aware of. That discovery led to a £100,000 contract for workflow automation, data pipelines and integration for the finance team. The work creates the foundations for AI to support further process automation.

This is where I make a commercial contribution: helping a customer recognise the challenge, understand its impact and see a credible route forward. Across discovery, tailored demonstrations and proposals, I turn that understanding into opportunities that can develop into sales and longer-term customer relationships.

At Simpson Associates, I have also explored use cases with North Yorkshire Council, City of York Council and Bradford Teaching Hospitals NHS. I built an AI-driven discovery tool to help identify use cases, suggest further opportunities and prioritise roadmaps. It supports the judgement needed to decide where to start and what needs to be in place first.

Alongside customer-facing work, I have helped define Simpson Associates’ AI strategy, go-to-market approach and positioning within the Microsoft ecosystem. Work on RFPs, RFIs and tenders has developed my experience of shaping complex public-sector AI use cases. I bring together the customer’s needs, a useful proposed solution and a clear commercial story.

roles.title: Presales AI Specialist
summary: Lead problem-led customer discovery across businesses, councils and NHS organisations, uncovering needs before considering AI.
Identified five finance challenges at Keltbray, leading to a £100,000 workflow automation, data pipeline and integration contract.
Help define AI strategy and go-to-market positioning, prioritise use cases and shape complex public-sector tender responses.
detail: Customer discovery and commercial opportunities. I speak with customers to understand their situation, problems, frustrations, the implications for their business and the outcome they need. I begin with the business challenge and establish where an intervention would create value before considering AI.

These conversations can surface issues that are not visible across the whole organisation. With Keltbray’s finance team, we identified five challenges, some of which their data team did not know about. That led to a £100,000 contract specifically for finance, covering workflow automation, a data pipeline and integration work. Those foundations create the opportunity to overlay AI and automate processes further.

I have also worked through use-case discovery with North Yorkshire Council, City of York Council and Bradford Teaching Hospitals NHS. My role is to draw out the operational need, clarify the opportunity and shape a practical next step for the customer.

To support this work, I created an AI-driven tool that helps build and identify use cases, automatically suggests further opportunities and helps prioritise roadmaps during discovery. It helps turn a wide-ranging customer conversation into a clearer set of options and priorities.

AI strategy and solution shaping. Alongside pre-sales discovery, I have helped define Simpson Associates’ AI strategy, its AI go-to-market approach and how to position the business as a leader in AI within the Microsoft ecosystem.

I contribute to RFPs, RFIs and tenders, shaping proposed solutions for complex AI use cases, particularly across local government, policing and healthcare. This involves connecting customer requirements, data and integration needs, workflow changes and the proposed role of AI in a coherent solution.

These two aspects of the role inform each other: customer conversations reveal where the need is strongest, while strategy and solution shaping help turn that understanding into a focused proposition, a prioritised roadmap and a commercial opportunity.
